title: Basic school-meal nutrition rules per meal
jurisdiction: Global default from public guidance; national standards replace it

rules.message: A school meal should carry at least one 80 g portion of fruit or vegetables.
rules.source: WHO Healthy diet fact sheet (at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day) spread over meals; 80 g portion convention

rules.message: Sodium above 600 mg in one school meal.
rules.source: Derived from the WHO sodium guideline (2012), scaled down for children by energy needs

rules.message: Free sugars above 10 % of the meal's energy.
rules.source: WHO guideline: sugars intake for adults and children (2015)

rules.message: Saturated fat above 10 % of the meal's energy.
rules.source: WHO guideline: saturated fatty acid and trans-fatty acid intake (2023)

rules.message: A school lunch under 450 kcal is likely too small for school-age children.
rules.source: Derived as about a third of daily energy for school-age children; national tables replace this default

rules.message: A school lunch over 800 kcal is likely too large for most school-age children.
rules.source: Derived as about a third of daily energy for school-age children; national tables replace this default

rules.message: A school lunch should supply at least 12 g of protein.
rules.source: Derived from reference intakes for school-age children divided over meals; to be confirmed by a dietitian

rules.message: No whole nuts in meals for children under five.
Food with undeclared allergens is not served in schools.
rules.source: Codex General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods (CXS 1-1985)

disclaimer: DRAFT derived from public guidance. Not medical advice. Energy and protein bounds are global defaults by age band and must be replaced by national school-meal standards. Must be reviewed by a registered dietitian before adoption.
